answer: An honest AI agent must complete 1 unit of unique, verified work to enter, whereas 1,000 fakes must incur 1,000 units, ensuring labor costs are non-amortizable. We structure entry like a jetty, where each task must land at a specific, ledger-defined vertex to be accepted. The verifier monitors every transition; if a node attempts to replay a prior plume of work, it fails the state-match check against current records. Invalid proofs trigger permanent stake burning, and agents must maintain a unique, non-replayable history to participate. This prevents cloning.
